design_summary.problem: One Mac holds work for two employers (e.g. GitHub orgs 'acme' and 'globex'), an open-source org ('oss-org') and personal projects. orch's single RAG store, session capture, PR digests and task lists currently mix all of them. Content from one employer must never reach a session working for the other; open-source docs should be readable everywhere. Enforcement must be in orchd code, never in prompts.
core_model: A space is the unit of separation. Each space owns bindings: GitHub orgs, local folder roots, web URL prefixes, chat tenants (Slack workspace, Teams tenant), and an outbound term list.

Space kinds: 'public' (readable from every space; only accepts content verified public or under a root the operator declared public; never sessions or agent notes), 'isolated' (one per job; reads itself, public, and any private space it explicitly lists; never another isolated space), 'private' (personal; like isolated, and may read other private spaces it lists).
Two isolated spaces can never read each other. A config that tries is rejected at apply time. Combining two jobs is an explicit operator 'merge' operation.

Every chunk and every orch record (cached PR, event, task, session record) carries exactly one space, or 'quarantine' (readable by no session) when it cannot be placed. Unplaceable content never defaults to public.

Roots nest like GitHub CODEOWNERS: the deepest matching root decides a path's space, and a nested root may only be stricter than every root above it (public < private < isolated; under an isolated root only the same space). Example: ~/code public, ~/code/willesq private, ~/code/company1 isolated.

Placement happens at ingest from the writer (a web page a session ingests takes the session's space). The operator can retag any source; orchd moves its chunks to the new space's collection without re-embedding, deletes them from the old one, and records a sticky override so refreshes keep the new space.

The org that owns a GitHub repo decides its space. Fork parents are ignored. When a checkout's folder root and git remote disagree, the stricter one wins (public < private < isolated); two different isolated spaces disagreeing is a conflict: nothing is indexed and the session gets no space.

Each space gets its own Qdrant collection, plus one for public and one for quarantine. The payload also stores 'space' as a second layer. Searches query only the collections the caller may read and merge them with reciprocal rank fusion.

A caller's space is decided by orchd: the kernel-reported peer PID, walked up the process tree to a harness process registered at SessionStart. A session is pinned to the space of its first cwd for its whole life. Request fields such as cwd never widen access.

A PreToolUse guard (plus CwdChanged logging) records every tool call, extracts its targets (cwd, file paths, cd destinations, git -C, gh repo targets) and refuses calls that reach another isolated space. Moving within the session's own space is allowed. Enforcement is on from the first release.

Defense in layers: orchd memory enforcement (all harnesses), the pre-tool guard, OS sandbox deny rules for other jobs' folders, harness permission rules for file tools, a separate GitHub account per job, and git hooks for outbound terms.

The command log is bounded: deleted 7 days after the session ends (or 7 days after the last event if it never ends), total size cap, refusals kept 90 days, hash-chained, credential-redacted, never indexed into RAG.

Policy changes are drafts until applied by the operator (the user at a terminal or in the app). The policy lives in orch.db as numbered revisions: anyone, agents included, may save a draft; only the operator applies one, naming the revision they reviewed. Callers descended from a harness or from orchd cannot apply. A pending draft, or an applied revision edited in orch.db outside orchd, shows as drift and changes nothing that is enforced.
With no spaces configured, orch behaves exactly as today.

Each enforcement layer (memory filtering, tool guard mode, outbound terms, sandbox rules) has an operator-only switch in the UI and CLI, optionally timed. Switching a layer off is logged and announced in every session's start digest; logging continues while it is off.

A session's liveness comes from the kernel: its pinned harness PID must still exist with the same start time. Idle sessions left open for days stay 'idle', never 'ended'; a process that exits without SessionEnd is marked ended within a minute. 'orch sessions list' shows every session, including running harness processes that have no pin.

Each job space has its own GitHub account (a gh profile directory, GH_CONFIG_DIR) from the start. orchd uses it for that space's docs sync, PR monitoring and reviews. The user logs in to each profile with gh themselves; orch never handles the token.
Spaces cover Claude Code and Codex. No Google harness is in scope.

Per-space harness settings (sandbox denyRead/denyWrite for other jobs' roots, Read/Edit denies, env GH_CONFIG_DIR) are written automatically into each checkout's local, uncommitted settings file; 'orch run <space> -- claude|codex' starts a session with the space's full profile from anywhere.
design_summary.labels: Chunk label = space x trust. trust already exists (assigned server-side by writer). This shape stays compatible with OpenAPPA's audience x trust if an integration is wanted later.

invariants.rule: No read path returns content, URIs or titles from a space outside the caller's readable set.
orchd alone decides a chunk's space and a caller's space. Client-supplied fields (cwd, filters, tags, space) can narrow results but never widen them.
Content that cannot be placed goes to quarantine, never to public or any other space.
Two isolated spaces never read each other. A config that would allow it is rejected and the last applied config stays active.
A session's space is fixed by its first cwd and never changes for the life of the session, including resume, compact and subagents.
Space policy changes take effect only through an operator-only apply. Callers descended from a harness or from orchd are refused.
Outbound terms never appear in logs, transcripts, refusal messages, error messages, the UI or indexed content.
A chunk whose labels_v is not the current policy's is unreadable until relabelled.
Derived content (summaries, session records, task results, files written by a session outside any root) carries the space of what it came from.
With no spaces configured, behavior is identical to today. The existing test suite passes unchanged.
Every cache that holds content or embeddings is keyed by space.
The command log is never indexed into RAG and is readable only by the operator, or by a session for its own events.
While the tool guard is switched on in an enforcing mode, it fails closed: timeout, unreadable pin or unreadable policy means refuse.
A nested root is never less strict than any root above it, and an isolated root never contains a root of a different isolated space.
Retagging moves data and never duplicates it: after a retag, the source exists only in the new space, the total chunk count is unchanged, and no new embeddings were computed.
Enforcement switches are operator-only, every change is logged with time and caller, and while any layer is off every session's start digest says so.

confirmed_by_user.decision: Content can be shared (readable from anywhere) or separated by where the caller runs. Separation is by folder or root location and is verified by orchd code, not by an AI.
Docs (GitHub owner docs, sources) must fall within the separation too, not only sessions.
An open-source GitHub org is readable from anywhere; two employer orgs must never bleed into each other.
Install a pre-tool-use hook that records every command; sessions keep their first directory and cannot circumvent it by changing directory.
The command log is cleaned up, e.g. 7 days after the session ends.
Configuration has a basic setup plus extensive user control in the app UI.
The design must extend to chat feeds later (Teams, Slack channels and DMs).
Use spaces with kinds public/isolated/private (was R-01).
Pin the session's space, not the exact folder; moving within the same space is allowed (was R-02).
One Qdrant collection per space plus public and quarantine collections, with the payload filter as a second layer (was R-03).
Enforcement is on from the first release, not after a log-only period. Every enforcement layer can be switched on and off from the UI so behavior can be isolated when debugging (replaces R-04).
Default guard mode is 'block other jobs'; 'strict' is opt-in; the mode is configurable in the UI (was R-05).
Do not adopt OpenAPPA as a component now; copy its patterns; consider an orch label source later (was R-06).

Content is placed by its writer at ingest: a web page a session ingests takes that session's space. The user can retag any source in the UI, and orchd moves its data to the new space (a move, never a copy) and keeps it there on later refreshes. This keeps the user in control and avoids duplicate data (replaces R-07).

Nested roots are allowed and resolve like GitHub CODEOWNERS: the deepest matching root decides. A nested root may be stricter than the roots above it, never less strict (e.g. ~/code public, ~/code/willesq private, ~/code/company1 isolated). The UI has a validator that shows which roots apply to a directory and the space it resolves to (replaces R-08).
A job (isolated) space may opt in to reading a private space such as personal by listing it in its reads. It is off by default and never extends to another isolated space (was Q-01).
The command log stores the full command text, credential-redacted and capped at 2 KB, plus targets and the decision (was Q-02).
Each job space uses its own GitHub account from the start: orchd's docs sync, PR monitoring and reviews for an isolated space's orgs run only with that space's gh profile (was Q-04).
Queued tasks may explicitly search chat channels in their own space, never DMs; nothing from chat is auto-injected into tasks (was Q-05).
No Google harness (Gemini CLI or Antigravity CLI) is in scope for spaces. Spaces cover Claude Code and Codex; the existing Gemini adapter is left as it is and reported as not covered (was Q-06).
The app shows all spaces at once, labelled, with a one-click screen-share-safe mode that hides everything except a chosen space (was Q-07).
Session content from a session pinned under a public root goes to a configured default space (e.g. personal) and can be retagged later (was Q-08).

Per-space sandbox rules, file-permission denies and GH_CONFIG_DIR reach agent sessions two ways: orch automatically keeps a local settings file in every checkout under a space's roots (no change to how sessions start), and an optional launcher, 'orch run <space> -- claude|codex', starts a session with that space's full profile from any folder (was Q-03, option D).

Keep one Qdrant collection per space (D-10) and accept its measured search cost: 1.5x (2 segments) to 1.9x (default segments) the p95 of one filtered collection, about +15 ms per hybrid search on 40,000 chunks (SP-002, docs/internals/memory.md 'Cost of a collection per space').

config.yaml was removed (settings live in orch.db, PR #142). The spaces policy is stored in orch.db as numbered draft and applied revisions with a content hash; SetSpacesDraft is open to any caller except queued tasks, and drafts record whether the operator saved them; DiffSpaces and ApplySpaces are operator-only and names the reviewed revision, and drift means a pending draft or an applied row that no longer matches its hash. SP-020.2.a3 reworded accordingly.

Accept SP-010's residual audit finding as a documented risk: a process started outside a session's tree under a kept-alive parent can take a new pin in its own directory. Pins grant nothing yet; access by a pin's space is gated on RC-01.

After an SP-011 test wrote to the real orch.db (migrating it from schema 22 to 25 and adding 301 test rows to session_pins), delete only the test rows and keep schema 25; the new tables stay empty until a release uses them.

reconvene.topic: Gate pin-based access on the tool guard
reconvene.detail: SP-011 and SP-025 must not grant memory reads by a pin's space until SP-041 stops a session from starting a harness outside its tree, or until there is stronger evidence of a real top-level harness (kernel executable path, session and tty checks). Today one command can start a fake 'claude' under a kept-alive shell and pin it in another directory (accepted risk, D-26).

reconvene.topic: Codex SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks
reconvene.detail: orch's Codex install registers no SessionStart or SessionEnd hook, so Codex sessions are never pinned. Proposal: register orch-hook session-start and session-end for Codex (D-20 covers Codex).

reconvene.topic: Bind the peer PID to its connection (proposed SP-011 acceptance item)
reconvene.detail: NearestAncestor trusts its starting PID; a peer that forks, hands its socket to a child and exits leaves its PID free for reuse under another space's harness. Bound the walk by the accept time, or identify the peer by kernel token (LOCAL_PEERTOKEN, SO_PEERPIDFD). Not found must mean no space, never a default.

reconvene.topic: Pins across orchd restarts on Linux
reconvene.detail: Optional: key pins on raw start ticks plus boot_id instead of wall-clock start time if pins must survive restarts on Linux.

reconvene.topic: Proof for non-GitHub or remoteless checkouts under a public root
reconvene.detail: A checkout whose remote is not on GitHub (GitLab, local-only) has no remote fact, so under a public root the root rule places it public. Decide whether such content needs proof before SP-023 writers use the classifier.

reconvene.topic: Confirm a specific GitHub node ID
reconvene.detail: --confirm-github-org accepts whatever node ID GitHub returns at apply time. Proposal: confirm org=node_id and show old, new and seen node IDs in 'orch spaces diff'.

reconvene.topic: Org identity checks on every GitHub ingestion path
reconvene.detail: Only docs sync re-checks org bindings. Sources, the review watcher and PR monitoring should call CheckOrg, and a long sync should re-check between repos. May fit SP-023 or SP-043 rather than a new feature.

reconvene.topic: Where the command log is stored
reconvene.detail: SP-014 does not say where the command log lives; orch.db is mode 0644. Decide the store and its file mode before SP-014.

reconvene.topic: SP-046 follow-ups and the shared /tmp channel
reconvene.detail: Write sandbox.enabled, allowUnsandboxedCommands=false and the Read(//...) denies together in the root settings.local.json and test that combination from a subfolder, plus Grep, Glob and Edit against the Read deny. SP-046.1 a5 needs a login in a temp profile (user step). Codex has no per-checkout path, so its coverage depends on the launcher. Codex ':workspace' still lets every space write the shared /tmp and $TMPDIR, a cross-space channel read denies don't close.

reconvene.topic: SP-063 follow-ups
reconvene.detail: Proposed: GitHub scopes for profile-only orgs; stricter gh_config_dir checks; refuse calls a space's profile cannot read; a quota cap for isolated accounts. Known gaps: profile-only orgs cannot be PR-watched yet, and the repo picker and PR-outcome tracker still use the default login.

reconvene.topic: SP-020 audit lows
reconvene.detail: Prune old draft revisions; normalise roots (NFC/NFD, symlinks) and web prefixes the way enforcement will match; clearer refusal when a bare node/bun/deno above 'orch' makes orchd refuse the operator, and don't count doubled '/' toward the depth limit; a session can keep saving drafts so the operator's apply is always stale; 'orch status' should say nothing is readable when the newest apply fails to verify; resolve root symlinks before nesting checks; transient changed_outside_orchd during an apply.

reconvene.topic: SP-022 lows
reconvene.detail: The repo lookup cache and its 30-a-minute budget are shared by agents and the operator (timing side channel; agents can starve the operator). Agent-supplied paths reach the handoff checkout reader, which has no timeout or concurrency cap. Paths match case-insensitively but URL paths case-sensitively, and IDN/punycode hosts are not unified. An applied policy binding both spellings of a web prefix to different spaces fails to load at the next orchd start.

reconvene.topic: SP-010 lows
reconvene.detail: The PinSession comment in orchd.proto says 'live pin' though the rule also applies to an ended pin; the registry lock is held while placement waits on GitHub (up to 10 s); a harness can claim a not-yet-pinned session ID first (denial of service only); the harness start time is read just after the walk; a session can end its own pin early.

reconvene.topic: Guard tests against the real data directory
reconvene.detail: internal/daemon tests that call db.Open() without setting ORCH_DATA_DIR use the developer's real orch.db (how RC-23 happened). Proposal: a TestMain in packages that open orch.db sets a temporary ORCH_DATA_DIR, or db.Open refuses the default path under go test.

reconvene.topic: Which space a queued task reads and writes
reconvene.detail: SP-011 resolves a task's process to its live run (task ID, directory, session) from the process tree; a reported orch-task-id only marks a caller as a task. No feature decides a task's space (the dispatching session's pin, the placement of its cwd, or a space named at dispatch), and a task whose run orchd is not tracking (a verification run, a run in another worker) has no record and so resolves to no space. Decide before SP-025 enforces reads.

reconvene.topic: A process that left its session's tree resolves to the operator
reconvene.detail: SP-011 resolves a caller with no harness above it as the operator, the widest result. A session process that double-forks, or starts a process through launchctl submit, open or osascript, before orchd accepts its connection, gets that result without a fake harness or a pin. This is wider than the D-26 detached-harness case. SP-025 must not grant operator-level memory reads by resolution alone until SP-041 (or kernel evidence such as audit tokens) covers it.

reconvene.topic: SP-011 audit lows
reconvene.detail: The resolved session ID is 'a session of this harness process' (subagent and /clear pins share the process), not necessarily the caller's own; SP-016 and SP-017 must not key per-session data on it without telling them apart (documented in docs/internals/daemon.md, Caller sessions). The start time of orchd's child on a task's path is read just after the walk, like the harness's (RC-13).

reconvene.topic: SP-011.2 cost bound on Linux
reconvene.detail: Resolving a new connection is p99 0.79 ms on the M3 Max but p99 6.5 ms on CI's shared linux/amd64 runner under the parallel suite; almost all of it is SP-010's process walk at accept (the pin lookup is about 0.05 ms). TestResolveCost enforces 5 ms only on macOS (50 ms elsewhere). Confirm the bound applies to the Macs orch runs on, or ask for the walk to be cut (one pass instead of three over the ancestry) so Linux meets it too.

features.title: Record real hook payloads across harnesses
features.summary: A throwaway logging hook captures SessionStart, PreToolUse/BeforeTool, PostToolUse, CwdChanged and SessionEnd payloads for Claude Code and Codex across directory-change scenarios, and turns them into committed test fixtures.
features.why: The pin and guard depend on how each harness reports cwd. Only Claude Code's behavior is documented, and only in prose.

acceptance.measure: scenarios runnable without touching the real ~/.claude, ~/.codex or ~/.gemini

Each event is one JSON line in <dir>/payloads/<harness>.jsonl, labelled by `scenario`; `summary` prints scenario/event/cwd/hook_cwd/tool per line; `clean` removes only directories carrying its marker.

checkpoints.title: Claude Code scenarios

acceptance.check: Record: plain cd within project; cd outside project; 'cd x && cmd' in one call; absolute path read; git -C; Read tool on an outside path; subagent in another directory; /cd; worktree enter; CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1 on and off; resume; compact.
acceptance.measure: scenarios recorded with observed cwd in PreToolUse, CwdChanged and the next PreToolUse

evidence: Recorded 2026-11-08 with scripts/hook-capture.sh, Claude Code 2.1.309, headless `claude -p` sessions in a scratch project (user approved headless runs on 2026-11-08). 13 scenarios with cwd observed in PreToolUse, CwdChanged and the next PreToolUse: C01 cd within, C02 cd outside, C03 cd x && cmd, C04 absolute path in Bash, C05 git -C, C06 Read tool outside, C07 subagent cd outside, C08 MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1, C09 =0, C10 resume, C11 compact, C12 EnterWorktree, C14 PreToolUse deny. C13 /cd: not available in headless mode ("/cd isn't available in this environment").

Findings: (1) cd within the project: CwdChanged(old_cwd,new_cwd) fires and the next PreToolUse cwd follows. (2) cd outside the project (C02, C03, C07) or any cd with MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1 (C08): CwdChanged fires with the new dir, then the shell is reset to the project with NO CwdChanged back; the next PreToolUse cwd is the project. CwdChanged's own cwd field was the new dir in C02 but the old dir in C07. (3) Absolute paths, git -C and Read file_path never change cwd; targets exist only in tool_input. (4) Subagent tool calls share the parent session_id and add agent_id/agent_type; a cd inside a subagent did not persist and fired no CwdChanged. (5) Resume restarts in the project root, not the last cwd (source=resume). (6) Compact: PreCompact(trigger=manual), SessionStart(source=compact), PostCompact; cwd unchanged. (7) EnterWorktree moves cwd into .claude/worktrees/<name> with NO CwdChanged. (8) PreToolUse deny (hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision=deny + reason) blocks the call; no PostToolUse follows and the model sees the reason. (9) Another PreToolUse hook (rtk) rewrote tool_input (ls -> rtk ls), visible only in PostToolUse: a guard must judge the input that actually runs.

features.title: Verify how harness sandbox and permission settings layer
features.summary: Determine which settings files apply to a session started in a subfolder, whether per-space CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR profiles work (including whether they need a separate login), and what the Codex sandbox can deny.

checkpoints.title: Claude Code

acceptance.check: With a temp home: a sandbox denyRead on a folder blocks 'cat' into it; a Read(...) permission deny blocks the Read tool; record which of user, project and local settings apply when launched from a subfolder.

evidence: Recorded 2026-11-08, Claude Code 2.1.309, 16 headless `claude -p --model haiku` sessions in scratch git repos under the session scratchpad (user approved 11 + 5 runs on 2026-11-08). The user chose 'use my real config read-only' over logging in to a temp profile, so the user layer is the unmodified ~/.claude/settings.json; its env key DISABLE_TELEMETRY served as the user-layer marker. Every other layer set a distinct env marker read back with `env | grep`.

Layering matrix: L2 from checkout root -> user, project settings.json, local settings.local.json. L3 from repo/sub with its own .claude/ -> user, ROOT local, sub project, sub local; root project NOT applied. L4 from repo/sub/deep (no .claude) -> user, ROOT local only; root project NOT applied. L6 (fresh repo2/sub/deep) confirms L4: user + root local only. L5 from a non-git child of a dir with .claude/ -> user only.

Sandbox: S1 (root of sbx1; project sandbox.enabled=true, allowUnsandboxedCommands=false, filesystem.denyRead=[jobB]; local denyRead=[jobC]) -> `cat` of both fails 'Operation not permitted', so project and local denyRead merge and project enabled=true overrides user enabled=false. S1c same repo -> Read tool RETURNED jobB's file: sandbox denyRead does not block the Read tool. S1b2 (sbx1/sub, --permission-mode default) -> both files printed, consistent with root project settings not applying from a subfolder.

Read deny: S2 (project deny Read(//<abs jobC>/**), sandbox on) -> Read tool error 'File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings'. S2b2 same repo, Bash `cat` -> 'Operation not permitted': a Read deny also feeds the sandbox's denied reads. S2c from sbx2/sub -> file read (project settings not applied). S3 single-slash Read(/<abs>/**) -> not blocked (resolved relative to the settings file). S4/S4b (deny in ROOT settings.local.json) -> Read blocked from the root and from a subfolder.

Separate login: L0 fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and L1 temp HOME both exit 1 with 'Not logged in · Please run /login', so a per-space CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR profile needs its own login; persistence of that login per profile was not tested (the user declined the temp-profile login). features.title: Session pin registry in orchd
features.summary: orchd records, per session: session_id, harness, harness PID and start time, first cwd, main checkout, space, policy revision, pinned_at, ended_at. Set once at SessionStart; never changed.
features.why: INV-05. Pins are the identity every later decision uses.

checkpoints.title: Schema and RPC

acceptance.check: PinSession RPC stores a pin; a second call for the same session with a different cwd leaves the original unchanged and returns it.
Session IDs are validated (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$); invalid IDs are rejected.
The harness PID is derived by orchd from the hook connection's process tree, not from the request.
acceptance.measure: test with a fake process tree

evidence: a1: TestPinSessionKeepsFirstPin (internal/daemon/pins_test.go) pins sess-1 in dirs[0], then calls PinSession again for sess-1 with dirs[1] while the harness reports dirs[1]: the response equals the original pin and the stored row keeps first_cwd dirs[0]. PASS, go1.27.3 darwin/arm64, 2026-11-08, commit 5e5aa84.

a2: TestPinSessionValidatesIDs: '', 'a/b', '../x', 'a b', 'a.b', 'é', 'a\nb', 129 chars and 'sess;rm' are rejected with InvalidArgument as session_id, as parent_session_id and by EndSession; a 128-char ID, a UUID and 'A_b-9' are accepted; exactly 3 rows are stored. PASS.

a3: TestPinSessionHarnessFromProcessTree drives peerCredentials.identify over a fake process tree (hook 901 -> zsh 902 -> claude 400 -> Terminal 30, plus an unrelated claude 401) and pins through the resulting caller: the pin records harness claude, PID 400 and 400's start time; PinSessionRequest has no pid or harness field (checked by proto reflection); callers outside a harness, with a failed walk, an unknown peer, no start time, or a replaced harness PID are refused PermissionDenied. Related, from the security audit: TestPinSessionChecksCwd (a new pin needs cwd == the harness's kernel cwd), TestNestedHarnessKeepsOuterPin, TestDetachedHarnessGetsNoNewPin, TestNewPinOnlyWhileHarnessIsNew. All PASS.

checkpoints.title: Lifecycle

acceptance.check: SessionStart with source resume, clear or compact keeps the existing pin.
A subagent (parent_session_id set) inherits the parent's pin and cannot set its own.
SessionEnd sets ended_at; the pin row stays for retention (SP-015).

evidence: a1: TestSessionStartSourcesKeepPin (internal/daemon/pins_test.go) pins sess-life in dirs[0], then sends PinSession for each SessionStart source with the harness reporting dirs[1]: startup, resume and compact (same session ID) and clear (a new session ID in the same process, as Claude Code's /clear does) each return the original first_cwd, space, harness PID and policy revision; clear records inherited_from sess-life. 4 subtests PASS. It also checks that a pin taken after the first session ended keeps the process's pin, and that another process resuming the session is refused. Hook side: TestSessionStartPinsEverySource (internal/hook/pins_test.go) shows each of the 4 sources sends the same PinSession request. PASS.

a2: TestSubagentInheritsParentPin: a subagent asking for dirs[1] with parent_session_id=parent gets the parent's first_cwd, space and harness with inherited_from=parent; a nested subagent still names the root; a later PinSession for the subagent without a parent keeps the inherited pin; a parent with no pin (FailedPrecondition) or pinned to another harness process (PermissionDenied) gives nothing and stores no row. Hook side: TestSessionStartPinsSubagentWithParent. PASS.

a3: TestEndSessionKeepsPin: EndSession sets ended_at to the fake clock's time; a second EndSession keeps the first time; the row stays with first_cwd intact and PinSession still returns it with ended_at set; another process (PermissionDenied), an unknown session (NotFound) and the operator (PermissionDenied) cannot end it. Hook side: TestSessionEndEndsPin (session-end sends EndSession even without a transcript). PASS.

checkpoints.title: Before spaces exist

acceptance.check: With no spaces configured, pins record space '' and behavior is unchanged (INV-10).

evidence: a1: go test ./internal/hook/ passes 172 tests (2026-11-08, commit 5e5aa84). `git diff --stat origin/main -- internal/hook/*_test.go` lists only the new internal/hook/pins_test.go, so every existing hook test passes unchanged, including TestSessionStart, TestDispatchAllEvents, the TestSessionEnd tests and TestRecordedPayloadsParse. Pinning is added in dispatch around the unchanged sessionStart/sessionEnd handlers and never blocks the session (TestPinHooksNeverBlock). orchd side: TestPinWithoutSpaces shows that with no spaces policy (and with no spaces engine) a pin records space '' and policy_revision 0; TestPinPlacesSession shows a space is set only under an applied policy (acme; personal under a public root, D-22).

features.title: Resolve any caller to its session
features.summary: For every RPC, orchd walks the peer PID's ancestors to the nearest registered harness process (PID + start time) and attaches that session's pin to the request context. Queued tasks resolve from their task record; the operator (no harness ancestor, not spawned by orchd) is marked as such.
features.why: INV-02, INV-05. An agent that runs 'cd elsewhere && orch search' must still resolve to its own session.

checkpoints.title: Resolution

acceptance.check: A CLI process whose own cwd is in another folder resolves to its ancestor harness's pin.
A reused PID with a different start time does not resolve to the old pin.
Broken lineage, unknown harness or unsupported platform resolves to 'no session' (public only once spaces exist).
Request-supplied cwd is ignored for resolution.

evidence: a1: TestResolveCLIToAncestorPin (internal/daemon/caller_session_test.go): identify over a fake tree (orch CLI 950 -> zsh 902 -> claude 400 -> Terminal 30), with the CLI's own cwd in dirs[1] where codex 410's session sess-c is pinned, resolves to claude 400's pin sess-a (first_cwd dirs[0]); a CLI under a nested, unpinned claude 420 also resolves to sess-a; after /clear the process's live pin sess-a2 is named. Related: TestResolveKeepsOnlyTheNearestHarnessPin, TestResolveCachesPerConnection. PASS, go1.27.3 darwin/arm64, 2026-11-08, commit 7229821.

a2: TestResolveIgnoresReusedPID: claude 400's PID now has a start time one hour later, so identify records the new identity and the caller resolves to 'none', not sess-a; a hand-built identity with an earlier start time also resolves to 'none'. For tasks: TestResolveTaskIgnoresReusedCLIPID (a task CLI PID 77 reused by a later task's CLI resolves to a task without a record) and TestLiveByProcess (internal/agentrun/live_test.go). PASS, go1.27.3 darwin/arm64, 2026-11-08, commit 7229821.

a3: TestResolveNoSession, 3 subtests PASS: 'broken lineage' (shell 902 missing mid-walk -> identify error -> none; a harness-walk error alone -> none), 'unknown harness' (CLI 970 under unpinned claude 401 -> none), 'unsupported platform' (errPeerUnsupported -> none; no start-time reader -> none). Also TestResolveFailsClosed (no peer, foreign auth, unknown process, unresolved context, nil resolver, unreadable pin store -> none). go1.27.3 darwin/arm64, 2026-11-08, commit 7229821.

a4: TestResolveIgnoresRequestCwd: through the unary interceptor, a DispatchRequest whose cwd is dirs[1] (where another session is pinned) from the CLI under claude 400 resolves to sess-a; through the stream interceptor, a call carrying 'cwd' metadata of dirs[1] also resolves to sess-a. The resolver reads no request field (callerResolver.unary ignores req). TestResolveOperatorAndTasks: a reported orch-task-id only marks a task and never selects a record. PASS, go1.27.3 darwin/arm64, 2026-11-08, commit 7229821.

checkpoints.title: Cost

acceptance.check: Resolution time per connection, with caching per connection.

evidence: a1: TestResolveCost (internal/daemon/caller_session_cost_test.go) re-executes the test binary as a program named claude, which starts a child; for 1000 new connections it runs orchd's identify over the real process table (procstat.Parent/ReadProgram/StartTime, walking to launchd) and resolves to the pin in a temp orch.db holding 301 pins. TestResolverOnSocket shows newGRPCServer resolves every call served over a real socket.

features.title: pre-tool-use and cwd-changed hooks (logging)
features.summary: New orch-hook slugs 'pre-tool-use' and 'cwd-changed', installed for Claude Code (PreToolUse, CwdChanged), Codex (PreToolUse). The Gemini adapter is not extended (D-20). This feature delivers the hooks and hands every event to orchd; SP-041 adds enforcement in the same release.
features.why: D-04. The hooks are the vehicle for both the log and the guard.

acceptance.check: pre-tool-use and cwd-changed parse every SP-001 fixture and hand each event to orchd; with the guard switched off they always allow.
Hook wall time from process start to exit, events handed off asynchronously.
With the guard switched off, a panic, bad JSON or unreachable orchd still allows the tool call.
orch install adds the new events for each harness: dry-run by default, idempotent on repeat, backs up modified files, preserves third-party hooks.
orch status reports per-harness coverage of the new hooks, and lists Gemini as not covered by spaces.

features.title: Tool-call target extraction (pure function)
features.summary: Targets(tool, input, cwd) returns {paths, cd_dest, git_dirs, gh_repos} from tool inputs and shell commands: cd, pushd, absolute and ~ paths, relative paths against cwd, git -C, make -C, env -C, gh -R/--repo, gh api repos/<o>/<r>, file tool path fields, Glob/Grep path.
features.why: Checking only cd is circumventable; the guard must check every target.

acceptance.check: Table test of command and tool-input forms with expected targets.
Paths are cleaned and symlinks resolved; worktrees map to their main checkout.
Go fuzz test over arbitrary command strings never panics and stays under the time budget.
acceptance.threshold: >= 60 s with no failure; < 2 ms per input

acceptance.check: Commands it cannot analyse (bash -c with variables, eval, base64) are flagged 'opaque', not silently empty.

features.title: Command log store
features.summary: orchd stores tool events (seq, ts, session, harness, event, tool, cwd, targets, redacted command capped at 2 KB, decision, rule, policy_rev, prev hash) in owner-only storage, hash-chained per session, chain head anchored at SessionEnd. Never indexed into RAG.
features.why: D-04, INV-12; evidence for replay (SP-047) and the Activity view.

acceptance.check: Events handed off by the hook appear in order per session; storage file mode is 0600.
Credential fixtures (gh, AWS, Anthropic, JWT, private key) in commands are redacted before storage.
Commands longer than 2 KB are truncated with a marker.
No code path ingests tool events into RAG (asserted by test over writers).
'orch spaces log verify <session>' detects a modified, deleted or reordered record.
Append throughput.

features.title: Session liveness and session list
features.summary: orchd decides whether each pinned session is still running from the kernel, not from hook events: the pin's harness PID must exist with the same process start time. States: active (process alive, a hook event in the last 30 min), idle (process alive, no event for 30 min or more; a session left open for a week stays idle, not ended), ended (SessionEnd received, or the process is gone, or the PID now belongs to a different process; ended_at is the time orchd noticed), unpinned (a running claude, codex or gemini process with no pin, e.g. started before the hooks were installed). A sweep runs every 60 s. 'orch sessions list [--all]' and a ListSessions RPC show harness, session id, PID, space, pinned directory, state, last activity, tool-event count and refusals. A resumed session (SessionStart source=resume in a new process) rebinds the pin to the new PID and start time but never changes its space.
features.why: Sessions are often left open without /exit for days. Log retention and pins must follow the real process, not the last message.

acceptance.check: With a fake process table and clock: alive with a recent event is active; alive with no event for 30 min is idle; alive with no event for 7 days is still idle.
A process that exits without SessionEnd is marked ended within one sweep (<= 60 s), with ended_at set to the detection time.
A reused PID with a different start time marks the old session ended and never maps it to the new process.
SessionStart with source=resume in a new process rebinds PID and start time, keeps the space and the first cwd, and sets the state back to active.
'orch sessions list' shows live sessions (active and idle) by default and ended ones with --all, with the 9 columns named in the summary.
Running harness processes with no pin are listed as 'unpinned' (found by process name, as procstat.FindByName does).
acceptance.measure: test with a fake process table

acceptance.check: Agent callers see only their own session's row; the operator sees all.
Cost of one liveness sweep with 50 pinned sessions.

features.title: Log retention sweeper
features.summary: orchd deletes a session's events N days after it ended (N = 3, 7 or 30; default 7), where 'ended' comes from SP-017: SessionEnd, or the process gone. A session whose process is still alive is never treated as ended, however long it has been idle; instead its log is capped at 50 MB, oldest non-refusal records first. Refusal records are kept 90 days. A total size cap (default 500 MB) deletes the oldest ended sessions first.
features.why: D-05. The log must not grow without bound.

acceptance.check: With a fake clock: a session ended by SessionEnd is deleted at day N, not before; a session ended by process exit (SP-017) is deleted N days after detection; an idle but alive session open for 14 days keeps its records; refusals are kept to day 90.
A live session over 50 MB drops its oldest non-refusal records first; the total cap deletes the oldest ended sessions first and never touches a live session.
Sweeping twice changes nothing the second time; chain heads of deleted sessions are kept.

features.title: Read the pins and the log
features.summary: 'orch spaces log <session>' (CLI) and the ListToolEvents RPC. Pins and liveness are listed by 'orch sessions list' (SP-017). Operator sees all; a session may read only its own events.
features.why: INV-12; evidence for debugging and for the Activity view.

acceptance.check: An agent session listing events gets only its own session's; asking for another session is refused.
A weekly summary command reports, per space, tool calls, directory moves and moves into another space.

features.title: Guard decision function
features.summary: Decide(policy, pin, enforcement, event) -> allow | refuse, plus a rule id, as a pure function with no IO. Guard states: off, log, block-other-jobs (default), strict, set by SP-070. Covers targets in another isolated space, other jobs' GitHub orgs, self-protection paths and opaque commands.
features.why: D-09, D-12. Pure and replayable, the OpenAPPA engine pattern.

acceptance.check: Table test of the directory-change cases: cd within the space; cd into another job; compound cd; absolute path read; Read tool outside; git -C; gh api and gh -R into another job's org; opaque bash -c; /tmp build; worktree; /cd; subagent; settings tampering; session pinned to no space.
acceptance.threshold: >= 14, all pass in each of 3 modes

acceptance.check: Decide is deterministic: the same inputs always give the same verdict and rule id.

features.title: Enforcement switches
features.summary: Operator-only switches per layer: memory filtering (on/off), tool guard (off, log, block-other-jobs, strict), outbound terms (on/off), generated sandbox rules (on/off). Stored in orchd with the applied policy, set through SetEnforcement and 'orch spaces enforce <layer> <state> [--for 15m|1h]'. A timed switch reverts by itself. Every change emits an event. While any layer is off, orch status and every session's start digest say so. Logging never stops.
features.why: D-11 and D-12: enforcement from the first release, switchable to isolate behavior when debugging.

acceptance.check: Each of the 4 layers can be set to each of its states; the default is memory on, guard block-other-jobs, terms on, sandbox on.
SetEnforcement is refused for callers descended from a harness or orchd.
With a fake clock, a timed switch reverts to its previous state at expiry and emits an event.
While any layer is off, the SessionStart digest of every session and orch status name the layer and since when.
With the guard off, tool events are still logged with decision 'not enforced' and the verdict the guard would have given.

features.title: Enforcing guard in orch-hook (fail closed)
features.summary: pre-tool-use decides locally from two read-only files orchd writes (applied policy plus enforcement state, session pin) and emits each harness's deny format. This is a documented exception to the hook never-block contract: while the guard is in an enforcing state, a timeout or unreadable input means refuse. The refusal message names the rule and never the matched text.
features.why: D-11 (enforced from the first release), INV-13.

acceptance.check: Deny output matches each harness's documented format (Claude Code permissionDecision; Codex per SP-001).
Timeout, missing pin and unreadable policy each refuse in enforcing states, and allow when the guard is off or in log state.
Decision latency including file reads.
Replay of the SP-001 fixtures under block-other-jobs.
acceptance.measure: refusals for targets within the session's own space

acceptance.check: Switching the guard off through SP-070 takes effect for the next tool call of a running session.

features.title: Self-protection paths
features.summary: The guard refuses agent writes to orch's config and data directories, the policy snapshot and pin files, terms files, ~/.claude/settings*, ~/.codex/hooks.json and config, Gemini settings, and .git/hooks. This covers file tools and shell redirection targets.
features.why: Otherwise an agent could remove orch's hooks or edit the pin. Pattern from OpenAPPA's file-tracker.

acceptance.check: Write, Edit and MultiEdit, plus Bash '>', '>>', tee, sed -i, cp and mv into each protected path, are refused.
Reads of protected paths other than terms files and credentials remain allowed.

features.title: Live GitHub guard
features.summary: gh and git commands whose target repo or org belongs to another isolated space are refused: gh api repos/..., gh -R, gh repo clone, and git clone/fetch/push to such remotes.
features.why: An agent with one gh login could read the other employer's org directly, bypassing memory entirely.

acceptance.check: Covered command forms are refused for another job's org and allowed for the session's own space and public.

features.title: Policy replay
features.summary: 'orch spaces replay <session|fixtures> [--policy <rev|file>]' re-decides recorded events and reports verdict changes. CI runs it over the SP-001 fixtures.
features.why: Policy changes are tested against real behavior before they apply (OpenAPPA replay pattern).

acceptance.check: Replay under the recording policy reproduces every recorded decision.
Replay under a changed policy lists each changed verdict with its rule id.

features.title: Minimal Spaces controls in the app
features.summary: Before the full Spaces pane: a Spaces section in the existing Settings pane (and the menu bar panel) with the enforcement switches and their timers, a banner while any layer is off, and a directory validator: type or pick a path and see every matching root from shallowest to deepest, the effective space, any git-remote adjustment, and why.
features.why: D-11 (switches in the UI from day one) and D-15 (directory validator).

acceptance.check: Each layer can be switched from the app; the change appears in orch status within 2 s; a timed switch shows its countdown.
Light and dark snapshots of the section and of the 'enforcement off' banner.

For the nested-root fixture (~/code public, ~/code/willesq private, ~/code/company1 isolated), the validator's chain and result equal ExplainPlacement for at least 8 paths, including a path under no root and a checkout whose remote is stricter than its root.

features.title: Stamp origin and space on every write
features.summary: All six IngestText writers record origin fields and run the classifier; the chunk payload gets origin.*, space and labels_v. Clients cannot set space; a client Ingest is placed in the caller's pinned space.
features.why: INV-02, INV-03; D-02 (docs follow the separation).

acceptance.check: One test per writer asserts origin, space and labels_v on stored chunks.
docs sync records repo visibility (add Private to docs.Repo) and owner node ID per repo.
A client-supplied 'space' or tag claiming a space is ignored; the chunk lands in the caller's pinned space or quarantine.

features.title: A Qdrant collection per space
features.summary: Each space maps to its own collection (plus public and quarantine). Writes route by space; searches query only the caller's readable collections and fuse with RRF. Migration, reindex, backup and hybrid tooling work per collection. Every content or embedding cache is keyed by space.
features.why: R-03, INV-11; physical separation removes 'forgot the filter' bugs and cross-space BM25/IDF statistics.

acceptance.check: A recording fake store proves writes for space S touch only S's collection.
A recording fake store proves a search queries only the allowed collections.
The payload filter on space is still applied inside each collection (second layer).
MigrateHybrid, ReindexKeywords and DropBackup iterate every space collection.
Each cache key includes the space; a hit cached for space A is never served to space B.
Search p95 against the SP-002 baseline at 40,000 chunks.

features.title: Enforce spaces on every memory read path
features.summary: Search, GetDocument, ListSources, ListDocs, rag_list_sources, session recall, auto-RAG and 'rag why' resolve the caller's readable spaces (SP-011) and apply them inside orchd. Caller filters are combined with AND. A registry lists every read RPC with its space decision.
features.why: INV-01, INV-02.

acceptance.check: Two isolated spaces plus public, 200 chunks each. From a session in space A, every read path, queried with verbatim text of B's chunks, returns 0 hits, URIs or titles from B.
acceptance.measure: cross-space results across all read paths

acceptance.check: Public chunks are returned to sessions in every space and to sessions with no space.
A caller filter (tags, source_uri, scope) can narrow but never add a space.
With memory filtering switched off (SP-070), cross-space results are returned and every such response is logged as 'not enforced'.
A job session reads personal only when its space opted in (D-16); it never reads another job's space either way.
A test fails when an RPC that returns stored content has no entry in the space-decision registry (like taskCallable).

features.title: Close non-memory bleed paths
features.summary: Events, the SessionStart digest, per-prompt updates, ListPRs, ListGitHubItems, GetPRDetail, ListTasks, GetTask and PR reviews carry a space set at creation and are filtered for agent callers. The operator still sees everything, labelled.
features.why: INV-01. The session-start PR digest currently lists PRs from every org.

acceptance.check: One test per path: a session in space A sees no item from space B.
A cached PR's space comes from its repo owner, and a review task runs pinned to that space.

features.title: Relabel and migrate existing content
features.summary: 'orch rag relabel [--dry-run]' moves stale chunks (labels_v not current) into the right collection using stored origin, source_uri, checkout tags and the session table. Unplaceable chunks go to quarantine. Resumable. Dry-run prints counts per transition, never content.
features.why: INV-08, INV-03; stale labels are the documented failure in other systems (Onyx #15990).

acceptance.check: Stale chunks are unreadable before relabel and readable in the right space after.
A second run changes 0 chunks.
An interrupted run resumes without duplicating or losing chunks (count before = count after).
Dry-run output contains only counts and space names.
Relabel of 40,000 chunks.

features.title: Retag a source (move its data)
features.summary: RetagSource RPC (operator-only), 'orch spaces retag <source_uri> <space>' and the UI. orchd copies the source's points, vectors and payloads to the target space's collection, verifies the count, then deletes them from the old collection. No re-embedding. It records a sticky override (source_uri -> space) that later refreshes and re-ingests honor. Retagging into public, or out of an isolated space, needs explicit confirmation. Resumable.
features.why: D-14: the user stays in control of placement, and data is moved rather than duplicated.

acceptance.check: After a retag, the source's chunk count in the new collection equals the count before, the old collection holds 0 of its chunks, and the total chunk count is unchanged.
The fake embedder records no calls during a retag.
Search from the new space finds the source; search from the old space does not.
A retag interrupted after the copy and before the delete resumes to a single copy, with no duplicates and nothing lost.
A later docs sync, sources refresh or client re-ingest of the same source_uri lands in the retagged space.
Retag is refused for agent callers; retag into public or out of an isolated space without confirm is refused.
Moving a 2,000-chunk source.

features.title: Quarantine management
features.summary: 'orch quarantine list|assign|purge' (operator-only), with counts in orch status.
features.why: INV-03 needs a way out of quarantine that only the operator controls.

acceptance.check: list shows sources and counts; assign moves a source to a space and records an override rule; purge is dry-run by default and needs confirm.
All three are refused for agent callers.

features.title: Derived content and taint
features.summary: Summaries are made from one session at a time and inherit its space. Task records carry the dispatching session's space, and tasks run pinned to it. Files a session writes outside any root are recorded with the session's space, and a later ingest of them uses it. The operator's explicit cross-space reads taint that session.
features.why: INV-09; Copilot-style label inheritance; OpenAPPA file-tracker pattern.

acceptance.check: The summarizer never receives text from two sessions in one call; its output lands in that session's space.
A task dispatched from space A is pinned to A, searches as A and its events are in A.
A file written by an A session in /tmp and later ingested is placed in A.

features.title: Public-space write gate
features.summary: Only verified-public content reaches the public space automatically: repos GitHub reports as not private in a public-bound org, allowlisted web prefixes from sources refresh, and files under a root the operator declared public. Session writers never target public; a page a session ingests takes the session's space (D-14). Visibility is re-checked on every sync; a repo that turned private leaves public before anything else is indexed. Only an operator retag (SP-071) can move other content into public.
features.why: The public space is read by every session, so it carries the highest bar.

acceptance.check: A private repo in a public org goes to quarantine (or the configured space).
A public-to-private flip moves the repo's chunks out of public in the same sync, before other repos are indexed.
Unreadable visibility is treated as private.
Session, summary, hand-off and client writers can never target public.

features.title: Visibility in status and 'rag why'
features.summary: orch status shows spaces, chunks per space, quarantine count, conflicts, drift and relabel progress. 'orch rag why' shows the caller's space and the collections searched.
features.why: Users and agents need to see the boundary to trust it.

acceptance.check: Status output includes the six fields; agent callers see counts only for their own space and public.

features.title: Outbound terms per space
features.summary: Each space may have a terms file (term or re:<regex> per line, case-insensitive, word boundaries), refused if inside a git tree. An outbound action is refused when its text contains a term from a space its destination (the target repo's owner) does not hold. Covers git commit message and staged diff, git push range, git tag -m, gh pr and issue create/edit/comment/review, gh api writes. Refusals give the term's line number and hash, never the term.
features.why: INV-07; the destination-based rule from the design.

acceptance.check: Parser and matcher table tests, including regex terms, case, word boundaries and invalid regex rejection.
A term in a staged file (not the message) is caught for git commit; a term in a pushed commit is caught for git push.
A test greps refusal text, the command log, orchd logs and status output for each fixture term.

features.title: Git hook helper for terms
features.summary: 'orch guard git-hook --install' adds commit-msg and pre-push hooks to a repo (or core.hooksPath) that run the same term check for any committer, including the user's own terminal.
features.why: The agent hook cannot see commits made outside agent sessions or obfuscated commands.

acceptance.check: Install is dry-run by default, idempotent, backs up and chains existing hooks rather than replacing them, and uninstalls cleanly.
A commit containing a term is refused; one without passes; an existing hook still runs.

features.title: Per-space harness settings: per-checkout files and launcher
features.summary: Two delivery paths (D-23). (1) Automatic: orch keeps .claude/settings.local.json in every checkout under a space's roots, holding sandbox.filesystem.denyRead/denyWrite and Read(...)/Edit(...) denies for other isolated spaces' roots plus env GH_CONFIG_DIR for the space's gh profile. It merges with the user's own local settings, re-syncs when roots, checkouts or the policy change, and makes sure the file is ignored by git (adding it to .git/info/exclude when no ignore rule covers it). (2) Optional: 'orch run <space> -- claude|codex' starts a session with a generated per-space profile (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and Codex's equivalent if SP-004 finds one), so it works from any folder. Both are switchable through SP-070's sandbox layer.
features.why: The OS sandbox is the only layer that holds against commands that build paths at runtime; GH_CONFIG_DIR gives agent shells the job's own GitHub account (D-18).

acceptance.check: Generated settings for a checkout in space A deny every other isolated root, deny nothing in A, public or opted-in private spaces, and set GH_CONFIG_DIR to A's profile.
Existing user entries in settings.local.json are preserved; repeat generation is idempotent; a backup is kept before the first change.
After generation, 'git check-ignore' reports the file ignored in every checkout; orch adds a .git/info/exclude entry only when no rule covers it and never edits a tracked .gitignore.
A new clone under a space root gets its settings file.
In a temp home, a sandboxed 'cat' of a file in another job's root fails, and 'gh auth status' in the agent shell shows the space's account.

'orch run <space> -- claude' sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (and GH_CONFIG_DIR) for the child process only, and refuses an unknown space or a space the current folder resolves outside of unless --force is given.
A session started with the launcher from ~/scratch gets the same deny rules as one started inside a checkout of that space.
Whether a separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR needs its own Claude login is documented from SP-004, with the setup steps.
Switching the sandbox layer off (SP-070) removes orch's entries from every generated file and leaves user entries intact; switching it on restores them.

features.title: Refusal events and notifications
features.summary: Each refusal emits an event (session, space, tool, rule, term line number or hash, no content) to the operator's stream and the app's Needs-you section.
features.why: Refusals should be visible without reading logs.

acceptance.check: An event is emitted for each refusal with the required fields and no command text.

features.title: RPCs for the Spaces pane
features.summary: ListSpaces, ScanSpaces (read-only scan of chosen folders for git remotes, plus gh org membership and repo visibility), ExplainPlacement, ListSessionPins, ListToolEvents, DiffSpaces, ApplySpaces (operator-only, revision-checked).
features.why: The app is a thin client; orchd owns the logic.

acceptance.check: Each RPC has handler tests; taskCallable and operatorActions are updated, and a test asserts ApplySpaces is operator-only.
ScanSpaces writes nothing (asserted with a read-only fake filesystem and a fake store).

features.title: Spaces pane: Overview and badges
features.summary: A new sidebar pane: space cards with bindings and counts, live sessions with pins, directory moves and refusals, and a needs-you strip (conflicts, quarantine, drift). Sidebar badge priority: conflicts, quarantine, drift, relabel progress. Basic/Advanced mode switch. A screen-share-safe mode hides every space except one you pick (D-21).

acceptance.check: Light and dark snapshots at the default width and at 320 pt companion width; no clipping (AdaptiveSplit).
The badge reflects conflicts > quarantine > drift > relabel in that order.
In screen-share-safe mode, no view model outside the chosen space contains another space's names, paths, PR titles or counts.

features.title: Basic setup wizard
features.summary: Five steps: Scan (checkouts by remote org, gh orgs, visibility), Spaces (plain-language kind per group: job, personal, open; nested roots shown as a tree with the stricter-only rule), Recall (safe defaults per content kind), Guard (enforcement switches and guard mode, on by default, plus log retention), Review (effect counts, then apply with Touch ID). Before apply, behavior is unchanged. The Spaces step asks for each job's gh profile and shows its login status.

acceptance.check: On a fixture machine (2 job orgs, 1 open org with one private repo, 1 personal), the wizard proposes 4 spaces with correct kinds and puts the private open-org repo in quarantine.
Cancelling at any step leaves orchd's applied policy unchanged.
Time to complete setup on the fixture machine, excluding the scan.

features.title: Advanced editors: Spaces, Access, Rules, Coverage
features.summary: Binding editor per space; write-only terms field (count and hash shown, never terms); reads matrix with locked cells for isolated pairs; per-content-kind policy table; the directory validator with a tree of all roots and their effective spaces; the 'where would this go?' tester; generated rules with match counts; per-harness coverage; enforcement switches; source list with Retag (SP-071).
features.why: D-06 'extensive control'.

acceptance.check: Locked matrix cells (isolated to isolated, anything to isolated from private or public) cannot be enabled through the UI model; isolated-to-private cells are switchable with a warning.
No view model or snapshot contains a term string (fixture terms searched).
The tester's results equal ExplainPlacement for the SP-022 cases.
The roots tree marks any nesting that the validator would reject, and the UI cannot submit it.

features.title: Activity and Review
features.summary: Per-session command log with directory moves and refusals; Review shows the pending config diff with per-line validation, effect counts, drift (a pending draft or an applied revision changed outside orchd), and Apply behind Touch ID or password.

Apply prompts for system authentication before calling orchd.

features.title: Palette, companion mode and CLI parity
features.summary: ⌘K entries ('Where would this go?…', 'Review space changes', each space), navigation only; companion strip shows the Spaces badge; every pane action has an 'orch spaces' CLI equivalent.
features.why: Consistency with app conventions and the terminal workflow.

features.title: Chat connector framework
features.summary: A connector interface that reports origin facts only (system, tenant, container, container_kind dm|group_dm|private_channel|public_channel|meeting, participants by stable ID). Per-container allowlist. Per content kind: DMs are stored and searchable on request but never auto-recalled and never given to tasks. Retention per space and kind. URIs like slack://<tenant>/<channel>/<thread>.

Connectors cannot set space or level fields (only facts).

plan_location.note: Status on origin/main is authoritative. A feature's status changes on its feature branch and reaches main when its PR merges.

progress_file.purpose: Live progress for the user and the next session. The plan's status only changes on main when a PR merges; this file shows what is happening now. It is never committed (listed in .git/info/exclude).

schema.updated_at: UTC ISO 8601, set on every write
schema.step: the session_procedure step being executed, e.g. '6. checkpoints'
schema.checkpoint: id of the checkpoint being worked on, or null
schema.checkpoints_done: ids of this feature's checkpoints with evidence
schema.note: one plain sentence for the user: what is happening or what you need from them
schema.history: list of {at, feature, event}, newest last, keep the last 50; append, never rewrite earlier entries

status_values.in_progress: a session has started it on its feature branch
status_values.blocked: cannot continue without the user; blocked_reason says why
status_values.done: every acceptance item met and independently verified; passes=true, verified_sha and verified_at set
status_values.superseded: retired by an explicit user decision; kept for history, never deleted

session_procedure: 1. Sync. In the main checkout (/Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator) run `git fetch origin`. Read the plan from origin/main: `git show origin/main:docs/spaces/spaces-features.json`. That copy is authoritative for status; local copies may be stale.

2. Pick exactly one feature: the first feature in ascending 'priority' whose status on origin/main is not 'done' or 'superseded'. Never skip it, never choose another, never work on two at once. Run one session at a time.

3. Look for existing work on it. First read the live progress file (/Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator/docs/spaces/progress.local.json): if it names a different session_id with status 'in_progress' and updated_at less than 30 minutes ago, another session is working. Stop and tell the user. Then check branches and PRs: the branch is feat/<id in lowercase>-<short-slug> (e.g. feat/sp-020-spaces-config); run `git branch -a --list '*feat/<id>-*'` and `gh pr list --state all --search '<ID> in:title'`.

3a. If an open PR exists whose plan copy already shows the feature 'done' with verification, it is waiting for the user to review and merge. Report the PR link and stop. Do not start the next feature.

3b. If a branch or open PR exists but the feature isn't done there, resume it: use its existing worktree under /Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator.worktrees/feat/..., or recreate it with ~/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/git_worktree_create.sh <branch> and answer 'y' to reuse the existing branch.
3c. If the PR was merged but origin/main doesn't show the feature done, or a PR was closed unmerged, stop and ask the user what happened.
3d. If nothing exists, run ~/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/git_worktree_create.sh feat/<id>-<slug> from the main checkout and work only in that worktree.

4. Preconditions. Every depends_on feature must be 'done' on origin/main, and no entry in decisions.open may list this feature in 'blocks'. If either fails, stop and tell the user. (Priority order makes the first case unexpected.)

5. On the feature branch, set the feature's status to 'in_progress', increment 'attempts', and set 'branch'. Commit (signed). Push, open a draft PR titled 'feat(spaces): <summary> (<ID>)' early, record its URL in the feature's 'pr' field, and register it in ~/.pr-watch.json. Write the live progress file now and after every later step, checkpoint, block or finish (schema in plan_location.progress_file); make sure docs/spaces/progress.local.json is listed in the main checkout's .git/info/exclude.

6. Do the checkpoints in order. After each one, record evidence (test names, command output, measured numbers, or 'confirmed by user on <date>' for manual items) in that checkpoint's 'evidence' array and commit. Update the live progress file (checkpoint, checkpoints_done, note, a history entry) at the start and end of each checkpoint.

7. Manual items need the user: ask them to perform or confirm the step and wait. If you can't continue for any reason (missing input, a criterion that is wrong or impossible, 3 failed fix rounds), set status 'blocked' with a specific blocked_reason, commit, push, and stop. Never move past a blocked feature. When you stop or need the user, the live file's status and note must say so.

8. When every checkpoint has evidence meeting its threshold, run every definition_of_done check yourself. Then spawn an independent verifier: a fresh subagent that gets only the diff (origin/main...HEAD), this feature's JSON, the invariants it appears in, and definition_of_done. It re-runs every test, command and metric itself and reports pass or fail for each acceptance item and each DOD check. It does not see your reasoning.

9. If the verifier reports any failure, fix it and verify again, up to 3 rounds; after that, set 'blocked'. If everything passes, set status 'done', passes=true, verified_sha to the commit that was verified, verified_at to the current UTC time (ISO 8601). Commit that change (signed) and push. Leave the PR as a draft; the user marks it ready and merges.

10. Never delete, renumber or reorder features, checkpoints or acceptance items, and never edit acceptance criteria (criteria_sha256 detects it). Only the user may mark a feature 'superseded'. If you discover new work, describe it under 'Proposed new features' in the PR body; it is appended to the plan, with the next free ID, only after the user approves.

11. Finish with a short report: the feature, its PR link, the verification result, what is waiting on the user, and which feature step 2 will pick next once this one is merged. Leave the live progress file with the final status ('done', 'blocked' or 'idle') and a note matching your report.

12. Record decisions as you go, until the last feature is done. A decision the user makes goes to decisions.confirmed_by_user with the next D-id and the date. Everything else that needs the user later goes to decisions.reconvene with the next RC-id: proposed features or acceptance items (also listed in the PR body per step 10), low or accepted security findings, deferred follow-ups, unverified assumptions, and actions the user must take. Give each a kind (decision, follow-up or user-action), topic, detail, source (PR, issue or session URI), raised date, affects and status 'open'. Reconvene items never block work; an item the user settles moves to confirmed_by_user (or becomes a feature) and its status becomes 'resolved' with a note. Before reporting in step 11, check that your session's items are recorded.
local_safety: This Mac runs the orch you are changing. Exercise install changes with a temporary --home only; never write to the real ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, ~/.config/orch, or any repo's git hooks.

Don't restart or replace the running orchd, and don't run `orch install` for real. For anything that needs a daemon or Qdrant, use a separate ORCH_CONFIG_DIR, ORCH_DATA_DIR, socket and Qdrant collection, and remove them when finished.
To capture harness payloads (SP-001), use project-local hook settings in a scratch repository and ask the user before launching each harness session.
Never read, print or store credentials. Use `gh auth status` only; never `gh auth token` or token files.
